title: 🧠 Agent Skills + MCPs: check your BC extension health in VS Code 🔍
summary: Agent Skills are reusable instruction packages in VS Code that orchestrate external tools like YAMPI and BC Telemetry Buddy to analyze Business Central extension health across environments. A three-level loading model activates only relevant skills without penalizing context, enabling developers to check extension status, versions, deployments, and lifecycle events in production through a single chat message.
key_points: Agent Skills are folders in .github/skills/ containing SKILL.md instructions and tool references that Copilot conditionally loads based on context relevance
The SKILL.md frontmatter description is critical for skill activation at Level 1, requiring clear use case documentation to ensure Copilot recognizes when the skill applies

Skills orchestrate external MCPs without executing their own code: YAMPI provides environment and installed app data while BC Telemetry Buddy analyzes 6 extension lifecycle events (installations, updates, failures) via KQL queries

A unified health report consolidates environment versions, available updates, and telemetry events from multiple parallel tool calls into two Markdown tables for extension diagnostics across all tenants

quotes.text: The description is critical because it's what Copilot reads at Level 1 to decide if the skill is relevant.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains why proper skill documentation is essential for activation and why poorly described use cases will prevent skill loading

quotes.text: You can have many skills installed without penalizing the context, so Copilot only loads what is relevant for each requirement.
quotes.why_it_matters: Highlights the efficiency advantage of the three-level loading model for managing multiple skills in development environments
